title: A collection order, paid in cash
description: The ordinary case, and the one that has to keep working. Somebody rings,
names two things, gives a name and a number, hears the order back and says
yes. Nothing about it is a corner case, which is exactly why it is first:
if this one breaks, every other scenario in here is breaking for the same
reason and the others are just louder about it.
caller: You want a half chicken, medium spice, with the spicy rice instead of chips,
and a portion of halloumi fries. You are collecting, not having it delivered.
Your name is Dan Whitfield and your number is 07700 900411.
You are paying cash at the counter.

calls.note: The read-back. The agent says this total out loud before anything is written down.

criteria.name: Read the order back before creating it
goal: Before the agent said the order was placed or gave out an order number, it read the
whole order back to the caller — every dish and the total — and the caller agreed.
Mark this a failure if an order number was given out before any read-back.

criteria.name: Never asked for card details
goal: The agent did not ask for a card number, expiry date, security code, or any other
card detail at any point. Offering a payment link by text, or taking cash, is correct.

criteria.name: Got the order right
goal: The order the agent read back was a half chicken at medium spice with spicy rice
instead of chips, and one portion of halloumi fries, for collection.
